kind: changed-items pass after the D-024/D-025 clarity re-edit (D-023 rule 1, D-024 'Screening'). It covers only the changed lines (content/revoice-clarity.json: hi l02 l03 l05 l07 l09 l15 l16 l19 l20 l22 and new l27-l32; en the same plus l21), the six supers su1-su6, the s18 tail with the moved handset lift and dial tones around l30, the l09 cut moved to 'Zero', and l15 now whole on s20. It also judges each of them as a first-time viewer would. It is not a full screening; screening.json (round 2, 8/10) stands for everything else.
gate: D-023: 7/10 and no blocking fault. Met in both languages.
verdict: Pass, hi 8/10 and en 8/10, with no blocking fault. Nobody has listened to this render or watched it in motion. The judgement comes from sampled frames, whisper.cpp transcripts and level measurements. All four of the owner's D-024 order faults are fixed on screen and in the mix. (1) Why she is there: l27 'Six weeks, not one complaint at my police station. So I took a token too.' is on her own face (s02), over the tokens on the wall and the one in her fist. (2) The cinema: su2 'Roopam Talkies cinema · Imlipur' on the first wide (s05), then l05 'Roopam Talkies Thana' and l28 'This is a shut cinema.' (3) The railway: l05 says 'railway line' in words, and su3 'The railway crossing' labels s10. (4) The reply to an unheard line: l29 'SHO sahab, there's a fake thana in Roopam Talkies.' now comes before Tripathi's 'Talkies?', and 'Arre' is gone. Names now come early. Nandini is named at 2.8 s, in speech and on a super (she was first named at 58 s before). Tripathi's role is spoken in l29 at 44 s, and su4 names him at 55.8 s (hi) / 57.1 s (en), where before he was named at 92 s. That makes l24 'SHO Tripathi said...' land as a payoff. Pushpa, never named before, is named by su5. Every line I checked now follows from something heard or seen. Tripathi's raised palm in s18 motivates l30 'Don't go over my head to DSP sahab', and l31 names the DSP before the phone voice speaks. 'Form is ready' sits over the pen and blank form in s09. 'Got a shield for it' cuts to the shield on 'Zero'. 'At your own thana, press conference...' plays over the ZERO CRIME shield. Three things hold the score at 8. First, heard_as lines are still unmarked in the subtitles, which D-024 asks for: l03 and l07 are Nandini's lines subtitled over Nirala's face, and the DSP lines have no label. With sound on, the voice makes the speaker clear, so this is not blocking. Second, a few glosses are tacked on: en l21 'The evidence room.' and en/hi l22 'of the ration godown'. Third, s02 holds a single still for about 9.3 s. None of the new lines reads as 'as you know' exposition. l02 and su1 say her name at the same moment, which is redundant but motivated: she is introducing herself at a counter.

In the review cuts I looked at changed-line cues on their shots. Each new line plays over its speaker's shot, except the lines marked heard_as: l27 on Nandini (s02); l28 on Nandini (s07); l32 on Nirala with the pen over the blank form (s09); l29 off screen over the empty bench (s12); l30 on the s18 two-shot, Tripathi's palm raised; l31 on her close with the handset (s19); l15 over the shield (s20); l16 on her close (s21); l19 on her close (s27); l20 on Nirala sliding the registers (s28); l21 on the Nirala/Pushpa two-shot (s29). You do.') are subtitled over Nirala's face. A muted viewer could take them for his lines; with sound, the female voice settles it.
changed_items.supers: All six are burned into the clean and the review cuts in both languages, with the right text: su1 'नंदिनी जोशी · Sub-Inspector' / 'Nandini Joshi · Sub-Inspector' on s02; su2 'रूपम Talkies · इमलीपुर' / 'Roopam Talkies cinema · Imlipur' on s05; su3 'Railway फाटक' / 'The railway crossing' on s10; su6 'इमलीपुर थाना' / 'Imlipur thana' on s12 with l29; su4 'दयाशंकर त्रिपाठी · SHO, थाना प्रभारी' / 'Dayashankar Tripathi · SHO, head of the thana' on s15 with l10; su5 'पुष्पा कुमारी · Head Constable' / 'Pushpa Kumari · Head Constable' on s16, upper. Each is 90 frames (3.0 s) except su3, which is 60 frames (2.0 s with 6-frame fades, so about 1.6 s at full opacity). Each sits inside its shot. The lower supers sit at about 60% of frame height, clear of the subtitle band (about 74-82%), and no super touches a face. su5 (upper) sits top left, clear of Pushpa's face, bun needles and knitting. su4 against the shield plate: at the first (hi 1682 / en 1719), middle and last (hi 1758 / en 1795) full-opacity frames, the ZERO CRIME plate stays in the top ~8% of the frame and su4 at ~60%. They never touch, across the push-in. su4 does sit over part of the peanut cone and his forearm, but the cone's top and the peanuts still read, so I propose no change. Note for the record: s15 carries ov_shield, so su4 is on a shot with a plot overlay, which is against the letter of D-024 ruling 3.3. Every b6 shot after s12 carries the shield, the plate is never touched, and the brief accepts this placement.
changed_items.s18_tail_and_l30: Sound order in both languages: handset lift at s18's head (hi 69.8-69.9 s, -30 dBFS peak 0.1 s window), then quiet, then l30 (hi 70.5-72.9 s; en 70.2-73.1 s), then DTMF tones 2 frames after l30's speech ends (pulses about -30/-45 dBFS, hi 72.93-74.07 s, en 73.2-74.33 s), all ending at the cut to s19. l31 starts 2 frames (hi) / 3 frames (en) after the cut. The s18 tail of 36 frames is in edit.json and the timeline. This matches the beat: lift, his plea, she dials anyway. Small mismatch, not a fault: s18 is one still with her finger already on the keypad all through l30. Also, l31 follows the last tone with no ring or pick-up beat. That reads as a stylised cut.
changed_items.l09_cut_on_zero: Measured onset of 'Zero' in the mix: hi 53.88-53.90 s against the s14 cut at 53.93 s (frame 1618); en 53.30 s against 53.33 s (frame 1600). Both within one frame. 'Talkies? ... एक FIR नहीं।' / '...Not one case.' plays on the s13 two-shot with Tripathi chuckling. 'Zero crime...shield' lands on the shield insert. s14 is 1.9 s in hi and 3.7 s in en.
changed_items.l15_on_s20: Whole line on s20 in both languages: hi s20 2424-2580, l15 speech 2429-2572; en s20 2425-2578, l15 2430-2570. l16 starts on s21 (hi 2585, en 2583). The phone voice over the ZERO CRIME shield ('...press conference at ten tomorrow. Second zero-crime year.') is the right picture for the line.

cold_viewer_read.b1_b2: 'Next! Token number seven.' over the token, then her name, rank and reason: the premise is clear by 12 s. l27 is the one line that explains her disguise; it reads natural, not expository, because it is said to the man at the counter.
cold_viewer_read.b3_b4: The place super plus 'Roopam Talkies Thana' plus 'This is a shut cinema' make the fake police station in a cinema unmistakable. 'Imlipur has only one thana. Mine.' -> 'This is a shut cinema.' -> 'And nobody in our force wears a cap. You do.' (over his cap) builds a case. 'Form is ready.' is a thin, deadpan bridge to 'Then kindly dictate: Thana has been stolen.' It reads as him ignoring her charges and treating her as a complainant. It works, and is the flattest of the new lines.
cold_viewer_read.b6: Fixed: the viewer hears the report before 'Talkies?'. 'Two years, not one FIR in my thana. Not one case.' glosses FIR in passing.
cold_viewer_read.b7_b8: Pushpa is named. The transfer line is answered by 'what is an SI for?'. Tripathi's 'Don't go over my head to DSP sahab' glosses DSP as his superior without a lecture. The DSP is identified by her greeting before he speaks.
cold_viewer_read.b10_b11: 'Nirala ji' tells us we are back at the talkies. en 'The evidence room.' glosses malkhana; it is tacked on, but Nirala, eager to help, is a believable source. 'Bhaiyaji, of the ration godown' gives the one identifying clause D-024 asks for. It is a little stiff in English; the Hindi 'godown वाले भैयाजी' is natural.
cold_viewer_read.ending: Unchanged lines now land. 'my own thana' is known to be Imlipur thana (su6, l27), 'SHO Tripathi' is the man with the peanuts (l29, su4), and 'before ten tomorrow' is the DSP's press conference (l15). So 'who do I arrest?' poses the real dilemma.
cold_viewer_read.language_parity: Hindi and English carry the same information on the same shots. Hindi is slightly more natural in l22 and l30; English adds the glosses Hindi does not need (l09 'Not one case', l21 'The evidence room').
